## Columns

One row per event. 32 columns. A row is identified by `game_id` + `event_seq`.

```{=html}
<div class="store-dict"><table class="table">
<thead><tr>
<th>Column</th>
<th>Type</th>
<th>What it holds</th>
</tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>season</td><td>string</td><td>Season the game belongs to, written like 2025-26.</td></tr>
<tr><td>season_type</td><td>string</td><td>Part of the season: regular_season, play_in, cup_final (the in-season NBA Cup championship game) or playoffs.</td></tr>
<tr><td>game_id</td><td>string</td><td>League game id, ten digits starting with 00; keep it as text so the leading digits survive.</td></tr>
<tr><td>game_date</td><td>date</td><td>Date of the game in U.S. Eastern time, as the league lists it.</td></tr>
<tr><td>home_team</td><td>string</td><td>Abbreviation of the home team.</td></tr>
<tr><td>away_team</td><td>string</td><td>Abbreviation of the away team.</td></tr>
<tr><td>event_seq</td><td>int</td><td>Position of the event within the game, counting from 1 in the order the league&#x27;s feed lists the plays.</td></tr>
<tr><td>event_num</td><td>int</td><td>The feed&#x27;s own event number; it is not always in time order, because corrections are numbered later, so sort by event_seq.</td></tr>
<tr><td>period</td><td>int</td><td>Period of play: 1 to 4 are the 12-minute quarters, 5 and up are 5-minute overtimes.</td></tr>
<tr><td>clock</td><td>string</td><td>Time left in the period as M:SS, with tenths of a second where the feed has them.</td></tr>
<tr><td>seconds_remaining</td><td>float</td><td>Seconds left in the period.</td></tr>
<tr><td>seconds_elapsed</td><td>float</td><td>Seconds of game time played when the event happened, counted from the opening tip across periods.</td></tr>
<tr><td>event_type</td><td>string</td><td>Kind of event: period_start, period_end, jump_ball, made_shot, missed_shot, free_throw, rebound, turnover, foul, violation, substitution, timeout, ejection, instant_replay, heave (an end-of-period heave charged to the team rather than a player, NBA from 2025-26) or other.</td></tr>
<tr><td>event_subtype</td><td>string</td><td>Detail within the event type. Shots: dunk, layup, hook, tip or jump_shot. Free throws: 1_of_2 and so on, technical, flagrant_1_of_2, clear_path_1_of_2. Rebounds: offensive or defensive. Turnovers: bad_pass, lost_ball, traveling, shot_clock, offensive_foul, out_of_bounds, violation or other. Fouls: personal, shooting, offensive, loose_ball, technical, flagrant, take, clear_path, away_from_play, double or other. Violations: defensive_goaltending, kicked_ball, lane, jump_ball, delay_of_game or other. Timeouts: regular, short, reset, official, challenge or other. Blank for other event types.</td></tr>
<tr><td>team</td><td>string</td><td>Abbreviation of the team the event belongs to (the first player&#x27;s team, or the team itself for team rebounds, team turnovers and timeouts); blank for neutral events.</td></tr>
<tr><td>player1_id</td><td>string</td><td>League id of the main player in the event: the shooter, rebounder, player who turned it over, player who fouled, player leaving on a substitution, or the first jumper.</td></tr>
<tr><td>player1_name</td><td>string</td><td>Full name of the first player.</td></tr>
<tr><td>player1_role</td><td>string</td><td>What the first player did: shooter, rebound, turnover, foul, violation, sub_out, jumper, ejected or other.</td></tr>
<tr><td>player2_id</td><td>string</td><td>League id of the second player: the assist on a made shot, the steal on a turnover, the player fouled, the player entering on a substitution, or the second jumper. From 2025-26 the feed names one player per event, so assists, substitutions and jumpers are matched from the description text and left blank when a name is ambiguous, and the player fouled is not available.</td></tr>
<tr><td>player2_name</td><td>string</td><td>Full name of the second player.</td></tr>
<tr><td>player2_role</td><td>string</td><td>What the second player did: assist, steal, fouled, sub_in, jumper or other.</td></tr>
<tr><td>player3_id</td><td>string</td><td>League id of the third player: the shot blocker on a missed shot, or the player who gained possession on a jump ball (from 2025-26 matched from the description text).</td></tr>
<tr><td>player3_name</td><td>string</td><td>Full name of the third player.</td></tr>
<tr><td>player3_role</td><td>string</td><td>What the third player did: block, tip_recipient or other.</td></tr>
<tr><td>home_score</td><td>int</td><td>Home team&#x27;s score after the event, counted from the made field goals and free throws up to and including it.</td></tr>
<tr><td>away_score</td><td>int</td><td>Away team&#x27;s score after the event, counted the same way.</td></tr>
<tr><td>shot_made</td><td>bool</td><td>True for a made field goal or free throw, False for a miss, blank for events that are not shots.</td></tr>
<tr><td>shot_value</td><td>int</td><td>Points the shot was worth if made: 3 or 2 for field goals, 1 for free throws; blank otherwise.</td></tr>
<tr><td>shot_distance</td><td>int</td><td>Shot distance in feet for field goal attempts, where the feed reports one; older seasons leave many shots at the rim blank.</td></tr>
<tr><td>shot_x</td><td>int</td><td>Shot location across the court in tenths of a foot, 0 at the basket; populated from 2025-26.</td></tr>
<tr><td>shot_y</td><td>int</td><td>Shot location out from the baseline toward midcourt in tenths of a foot, 0 at the basket; populated from 2025-26.</td></tr>
<tr><td>description</td><td>string</td><td>The league&#x27;s own text for the play; when a play has a second note (a block or a steal) the two are joined with a vertical bar.</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
```

## Source and method

Compiled by Slam Dunk Bets from the NBA's official game statistics play-by-play feed. The league changed the feed's layout over the years; every season here is converted to the same columns, and columns the older feed lacks are blank for those seasons, as the column descriptions say.

The same file layout, IDs and column names are used for every season, so seasons stack without cleanup. See [how the store works](help.qmd) for formats, delivery and the license.

::: {.faq-item}
### How do the NBA files join to each other?

On the ID columns. Game, team and player IDs are the same strings in every NBA file and every season, so a join on `game_id` (plus `team` or `player_id` where the grain needs it) lines them up.
:::

::: {.faq-item}
### Which games are included?

Every regular-season, play-in, Cup final and playoff game, from the official box scores and play-by-play. Regular season and postseason sit in the same file, told apart by `season_type`. Preseason and All-Star games are left out.
:::
